title: Marketplace Listing Messaging Framework (AWS + GCP)
author: Soojin Lee
body:
## Purpose
This page defines the positioning and copy blocks for Redwood Inference’s AWS Marketplace and Google Cloud Marketplace listings.

Use it to:
- Keep listing copy consistent across AWS/GCP, Redwood Console, and Sales/SE enablement.
- Provide persona-specific value props and proof points.
- Prevent over-claims in security/compliance language (aligns with Security FAQ + security packet).

**In scope:** Hosted API, Dedicated, Private (VPC/on-prem), and compliance add-ons (e.g., extended retention, premium SLA—only where SKU/package exists).

**Owner:** Product Marketing (Soojin Lee)

---

## Messaging pillars (the “why Redwood”)
1) **Production economics you can control**
   - Clear levers to balance latency, throughput, and unit cost.
   - Tooling for batching/caching/routing and token-level visibility.

2) **Unified inference across environments**
   - Same API and operational model across hosted, dedicated capacity, and private deployments.
   - Move from pilot to enterprise procurement without re-platforming.

3) **Reliable by design (graceful degradation)**
   - Policy-based routing and fallbacks keep apps online when capacity is constrained.
   - Observability and rollouts reduce operational risk.

4) **Enterprise-ready procurement without losing developer velocity**
   - Marketplace purchase paths map cleanly to Redwood orgs/entitlements.
   - Clear onboarding steps + support playbooks reduce activation delays.

---

## Core positioning statement (internal)
**Redwood Inference is a developer-first platform for running and optimizing LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments—delivering predictable latency and cost with production-grade reliability and operational tooling.**

### 1-liner (external / listing header)
**High-performance LLM inference with predictable latency, cost, and deployment flexibility.**

### Elevator pitch (external / long description intro)
Redwood Inference helps engineering teams ship LLM features with consistent performance across hosted API, dedicated capacity, and private deployments (VPC/on-prem). Redwood combines a high-throughput serving runtime with routing, caching/batching controls, and production observability—so you can hit latency SLOs and manage unit economics without building and operating the full inference stack.

---

## Differentiators (approved proof points)
Use these as bullets in listings, decks, and Marketplace FAQs.

### Performance + cost
- GPU-optimized serving runtime with modern attention optimizations and continuous batching.
- Cost/latency visibility with token-level breakdowns and per-model/per-route dashboards.
- Workload-aware batching/caching guidance and guardrails (Redwood Optimize).

### Reliability + operations
- Rollouts: canary deploys, A/B tests, and fallback policies.
- Smart routing by policy (latency/cost/region/tier) with graceful degradation patterns.
- SLA-backed options available on Dedicated/Premium packages (where contracted/sku’d).

### Deployment flexibility
- Hosted API for fastest time-to-value.
- Dedicated GPU pools for predictable throughput and data isolation.
- Private deployments for regulated workloads (VPC/on-prem options).

### Enterprise procurement & governance
- Marketplace-friendly procurement (committed spend / invoicing via cloud provider).
- Audit logs and access controls appropriate for enterprise environments (details governed by Security FAQ).

---

## Persona-based messaging (copy selection guide)
Use the sections below to tailor the listing emphasis (headline, first 2–3 bullets, and FAQ ordering) depending on the primary buyer.

| Persona | Primary pain | What to emphasize | Proof points to include | Suggested CTA |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **ML/Platform Engineering** | Serving performance, stability under load, rollout risk | Runtime performance, routing/fallback, observability, rollouts | Continuous batching, token-level metrics, canary + fallback | “Deploy and validate in minutes” |
| **Application Engineering / Dev Lead** | Developer velocity; integration friction | Simple API/SDK, model catalog, streaming + structured outputs | REST/SDK, streaming, tool calling/structured output support | “Start with Hosted API; scale to Dedicated” |
| **Security / GRC** | Data protection, auditability, evidence | Encryption, audit logs, shared responsibility clarity, NDA evidence flow | KMS/KMS-integrations, audit logging, SOC 2 report handling (under NDA) | “Request security packet / schedule review” |
| **Procurement / Finance** | Spend control; vendor consolidation; invoicing | Marketplace purchase benefits; predictable billing & entitlements | Clear SKUs, mapping to org/entitlements, support path | “Purchase via Marketplace; activate in Console” |

---

## Copy blocks (ready-to-use)
These blocks are intentionally modular to fit AWS and GCP formatting constraints. Keep claims factual and align with current product capabilities.

### A) Marketplace headline options (pick one)
1. **Predictable LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments**
2. **High-performance LLM inference with cost and latency controls**
3. **Developer-first LLM inference optimized for production economics**

### B) Short description (1–2 sentences)
Redwood Inference is a developer-first platform for running and optimizing LLM inference across hosted API, dedicated capacity, and private deployments. Achieve predictable latency and unit costs with production observability, rollouts, and policy-based routing.

### C) Top bullets (use 4–6)
- **Consistent performance across environments:** hosted, dedicated, and private deployments with a unified API.
- **Production-grade reliability:** smart routing, graceful fallbacks, and rollout controls (canary/A-B).
- **Optimize unit economics:** batching/caching guidance plus token-level cost and latency breakdowns.
- **Enterprise-ready governance:** audit logging and security controls aligned to enterprise requirements.
- **Fast onboarding:** marketplace purchase → entitlement activation → org linking in Redwood Console.
- **Flexible capacity options:** dedicated GPU pools for predictable throughput and data isolation.

### D) Long description (AWS-friendly)
Redwood Inference helps teams deploy LLM inference with predictable latency, throughput, and cost—without building and operating the full serving stack. Use Redwood Hosted API to integrate quickly, scale with Dedicated capacity for predictable performance and data isolation, or deploy Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem options) for regulated workloads.

Redwood combines a GPU-optimized serving runtime with production operations: policy-based routing, caching/batching controls, token-level observability, and rollout tooling (canary, A/B testing, and fallback). Marketplace procurement supports enterprise buying workflows while preserving a developer-first activation path in the Redwood Console.

### E) Long description (GCP-friendly; includes “how it works” tone)
Redwood Inference provides a unified LLM inference platform across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. After purchasing via Cloud Marketplace, you’ll link your cloud account to a Redwood organization in the Redwood Console to activate entitlements and begin sending requests using Redwood’s API/SDK.

Redwood is designed for production workloads: high-throughput serving, workload-aware batching/caching, policy-based routing, and operational tooling for safe rollouts and fast troubleshooting. Use Hosted API for rapid iteration, Dedicated for predictable capacity and isolation, and Private deployments for regulated environments.

---

## Marketplace-specific guidance
### AWS Marketplace formatting notes
- Lead with **headline + 4–6 bullets**.
- Keep “how to activate” steps in a short section (buyers often scan and rely on screenshots).
- Use AWS keywords that map to buyer intent (see suggested keywords below).

### GCP Marketplace formatting notes
- Include explicit **deployment/activation steps** and a lightweight FAQ.
- Avoid heavy jargon; emphasize how purchase maps to activation in Redwood Console.

---

## Keywords (approved list)
Use in listings and metadata fields where allowed.

**Primary keywords:** LLM inference, model serving, GPU inference, low latency, batching, caching, observability, dedicated capacity, private deployment, VPC deployment, on-prem deployment

**Secondary keywords:** token analytics, cost optimization, routing, fallback, rollouts, canary deployment, enterprise procurement, marketplace billing

**Avoid/limit:** “zero downtime” (too absolute), “guaranteed lowest cost” (not defensible), “fully compliant” (too broad).

---

## Competitive framing (what we can say)
Keep this customer-centric and avoid naming competitors in Marketplace copy.

### Approved framing
- “Unified inference across hosted, dedicated, and private environments.”
- “Production operations for LLM serving: routing, rollouts, and observability.”
- “Tools to manage inference economics while meeting latency goals.”

### Not approved
- “Best-in-class performance” without a cited benchmark.
- “Drop-in replacement for X” (creates support and legal risk).

---

## Security & compliance language: DO / DON’T
Security claims must match the Security FAQ and the current security packet. When in doubt, route copy to **Marcus Lin** (Security Eng) and **Olga Petrov** (GRC) before external publication.

### DO (approved patterns)
- **Shared responsibility:** “Redwood provides controls for encryption, access management, and audit logging; customers are responsible for configuration and usage within their cloud environment.”
- **Evidence handling:** “SOC 2 report and additional evidence are available upon request under NDA.”
- **Encryption:** “Data is encrypted in transit and at rest (service-specific details available in the security packet).”
- **Audit logs:** “Audit logs are available for key administrative events (scope described in our security documentation).”
- **SSO:** “SSO/SAML support is available for eligible plans (see documentation).”
- **Retention wording:** “Retention is configurable for certain logs/telemetry based on package and customer requirements.”
- **Residency wording:** “Regional deployment options are available; data handling depends on the deployment mode and selected region.”

### DON’T (disallowed / high-risk)
- “HIPAA compliant,” “PCI compliant,” “FedRAMP authorized,” or similar unless Legal + GRC have explicitly approved for the specific listing and there is a published program.
- “We never store customer data” (often false due to logs/telemetry, support artifacts, or optional features).
- “All data stays in the customer’s VPC” unless the SKU is explicitly Private/VPC and the architecture statement is accurate for the specific purchase path.
- “End-to-end encryption where Redwood cannot access keys” unless this is the implemented and documented mode (avoid ambiguous claims).
- “Guaranteed” statements (e.g., “guaranteed latency,” “guaranteed uptime”) unless tied to an explicit SLA in the customer’s contract/SKU terms.

### Required disclaimer (recommended in Security FAQ / attachments)
“Security and compliance information is provided for informational purposes and may vary by deployment mode and configuration. Contact Redwood to request the latest security documentation and evidence.”

---

## FAQ snippets (for listings + buyer enablement)
Use these in listing FAQs and keep answers consistent with docs.

**Q: How does a Marketplace purchase map to Redwood entitlements?**
A: After purchase, you link your cloud account to a Redwood organization in the Redwood Console. Entitlements activate for that org and determine which products/add-ons are enabled.

**Q: Can we use Marketplace procurement for Dedicated or Private deployments?**
A: Yes. Marketplace SKUs map to Dedicated/Private entitlements where offered. Redwood will confirm region, capacity, and deployment requirements during activation.

**Q: What happens if entitlements don’t activate immediately?**
A: Entitlements typically activate shortly after purchase. If activation is delayed, Redwood Support can validate the Marketplace event and resolve mapping issues. See the troubleshooting guide.

**Q: Do you support audit logs and SSO?**
A: Audit logging and SSO/SAML are available depending on plan/package. Request the security packet for current scope and configuration details.

**Q: Where is data stored / how does residency work?**
A: Data handling depends on deployment mode (Hosted, Dedicated, Private) and selected region. Redwood provides regional deployment options subject to availability; details are documented in the security packet.

---

## Call-to-action (CTA) options
Pick one primary CTA and one secondary CTA.

**Primary CTA options:**
- “Purchase via Marketplace and activate in minutes”
- “Buy now; link your organization in the Redwood Console”
- “Get started with Hosted API; upgrade to Dedicated/Private”

**Secondary CTA options:**
- “Request the security packet (NDA)”
- “Contact Sales for Dedicated/Private sizing”
- “View onboarding and troubleshooting docs”

---

## Screenshot/diagram captions (suggested)
- “Link your Marketplace account to a Redwood organization to activate entitlements.”
- “Monitor latency and cost with token-level breakdowns and per-model dashboards.”
- “Configure routing and fallback policies for reliability under load.”

---

## Review & publishing workflow (required)
1) PMM drafts copy updates and highlights any new claims (especially security/compliance).
2) Security review: **Marcus Lin** + **Dr. Aisha Rahman** for claim accuracy and evidence availability.
3) GRC review: **Olga Petrov** for SOC 2 / evidence handling language.
4) Sales/SE review: **Jordan Blake** + **Markus Klein** for field clarity and objection handling.
5) Partnerships submits to AWS/GCP portals after approvals.

**Change control note:** Marketplace listings are considered externally published content. Do not ship copy changes that materially alter security/compliance claims without Security + GRC sign-off.

---
